findings.finding: A satellite cellular network still being built: today's revenue is gateway hardware sold to MNOs near cost (Q2 2026 products 24.4M at ~8% margin) and U.S. Government milestone services (7.1M); no SpaceMobile service revenue has been recognized. Future revenue is a wholesale revenue share with MNOs that starts only when coverage begins (about 45 satellites).

Growth from 70.9M (FY2025) to the 150-200M FY2026 guide is mix, not structure: one-time gateway sales and government awards (over 125M new U.S. Government awards in Q2; ~50 gateways in the pipeline). The structural step (service revenue share) has not started; RPO 1.2B is mostly after activation, only ~6.6% within 12 months of 2026-06-30, and excludes the variable MNO revenue share.

Demand is MNO partners (over 60 signed, ~3B subscribers covered) plus an advance payment under a commercial service agreement (contract liabilities 266.9M) and U.S. Government awards; customer concentration by share is not disclosed. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon announced a D2D joint venture on 2026-10-02, which pools channel power on the buyer side.

Deployment guidance slipped twice: 45-60 satellites by end-2026 (2026-03-02), ~45 by end-2026 (2026-05-11), ~45 in early 2027 (2026-08-10). 13 were in orbit on 2026-08-10; BlueBird 7 was lost (125.9M write-off); no launch after August was confirmed by 2026-11-01 and the New Glenn launcher was lost in May 2026. Reaching ~45 needs ~32 more satellites; capacity is up to 6 a month and 10 launches are booked with two providers.

Revenue: one real period (H2 2025 guided 50-75M, actual 69.0M, ratio 1.10) - too thin to adjust by. Opex: guide raised from 70-80M to ~100M a quarter average and actuals ran above the guided midpoint twice. Capex Q2 inside its 575-650M range. Revenue guidance is credible so far; cost and timing guidance are not.

FY2025 operating loss is 287.7M (revenue 70.9M less operating expenses 358.6M per the 10-K); the prefetched pf_operating_income_fy2025 of -425.3M does not tie and must not be used. Q2 2026 one-offs: 125.9M BB7 involuntary conversion loss (non-cash), H1 induced conversion expense ~89M. SBC jumped to 63.5M in Q2 2026 (10.5M a year earlier) and is excluded from adjusted opex: it is a real recurring cost.

Spendable cash at 2026-06-30 is 2,288.3M of cash and cash equivalents (money-market funds are inside it, not a separate investment line); 434.6M restricted cash is not spendable (428.4M collateralizes the 420M UBS loan). At 2025-12-31 the 2.0B 'short-term investments' figure is the cash-equivalent part of cash, so cash + STI double counts. Pro forma for the July 2026 1.15B 2034 notes, management cites over 3.7B including restricted cash.

The build is funded by convertibles (~3.70B principal after July 2026: 2032 2.375% conv ~72, 2036 2.00% effective ~96, 2036 2.25% conv ~116, 2034 1.625% conv ~80 effective ~149, plus 3.5M at ~27) and an 800M ATM fully used and terminated in March 2026. Economic shares rose from ~256M diluted average in FY2025 to 389.2M at 2026-08-06; FCF was -694.8M in Q2 2026 alone. Purchase commitments 775-795M. Any delay extends the burn and points to more converts or equity.

Piotroski 4/8 (mixed); Altman Z'' 2.87 ('safe') is weak for a young cash-rich builder whose cash is debt-funded; ROIC -26.6% last year and incremental ROIC -12.5%; Rule of 40 not applicable; Beneish unavailable. All carried to the bear: value creation is unproven at any scale.

520M paid for the Ligado/L-band deal is refundable through a 520M backstop only if regulatory approvals fail; approvals are pending and litigation with Inmarsat may affect them; a further 30M is due at closing and ~81M a year of L-band payments may be settled in shares.

economics.reason: Not a demand cycle: a network build stepping from no service to contracted wholesale service; the risks are execution (satellites, launches, spectrum), adoption and funding, carried in the scenarios.

type.override_reason: Computed type confirmed: pre-service network builder with large losses on a very early revenue base. 'fast_grower' describes the revenue step only; the questions are deployment, adoption, unit economics and funding, and the valuation lens is a dated build-out path with explicit financing, not a multiple of today's revenue.

gaps: MNO revenue-share percentage, ARPU and paid capacity per satellite undisclosed: service revenue beyond FY2027 rests on consensus points, not a bottom-up build
